sites.name: IM-2 Athena landing point (Mons Mouton region)
sites.coordinate_frame: Lunar Mean Earth/polar axis (ME) body-fixed frame, planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude. ASSUMED: the LROC page does not name its frame; LRO products use the ME frame by project convention. Horizons interprets the submitted coordinates in MOON_ME (DE421-based).
sites.coordinate_source_title: LROC: IM-2 Athena Seen Obliquely (M. Robinson, 10 March 2025) - gives 84.7906° S, 29.1957° E
sites.surface_elevation_reference: Height above the 1737.4 km LOLA reference sphere, LDEM_80S_20M (PDS LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0 V2.0) bilinear at the site; verified against 1131 LOLA RDR shots (DEM - shot mean -0.26 m, sd 0.67 m). See data/terrain/site_elevation_report.json.
sites.horizons_altitude_reference: Height above the Horizons reference body for the Moon: a 1737.4 km sphere (response header 'Center radii'), the same reference as LOLA heights.
sites.altitude_conversion_note: horizons_site_altitude_km = (surface_elevation_m + observer_height_above_surface_m) / 1000 = (5321.9 m + 1 m) / 1000 = 5.3229 km. Both heights are relative to the same 1737.4 km sphere, so no datum conversion is needed. Surface value uncertainty: ~1 m for the stated coordinates; ~+/-5 m if the site coordinate is uncertain by 100 m (terrain within 100 m spans -4.4 to +4.6 m).

terrain.source: PDS Geosciences Node, LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0, polar products V2.0 (LOLA data through 2017-02-02)
terrain.rule: Use LDEM_80S_20M wherever the ray is inside it; continue rays that leave it (azimuths ~320-351 deg, 165-190 km) in LDEM_75S_60M. Stop a ray only when terrain at the global LOLA maximum height (+100 m) could no longer exceed the running horizon. If a ray leaves every file first, that azimuth's horizon is null (unknown), never flat.
